PullRequest.Title: Agents - Add multi-file diff action to pull request rows
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request introduces a new action to the pull request rows in the session chat input toolbar, allowing users to open changes from a pull request in the multi-file diff editor. 

### Changes made:
- Added an **Open Pull Request Changes** action to each PR row in `sessionChatInputToolbar.ts`.
- Implemented a new resolver, `PullRequestChangesMultiDiffSourceResolver`, to handle fetching and displaying the changes in the multi-file diff editor.
- Updated existing tests and created new tests to ensure the functionality works as expected.
- Adjusted the order of actions in the PR row to ensure the new action appears first, ahead of the "Copy URL" action.
- Enhanced error handling to display messages in the editor area for load failures and empty file lists.

### Validation:
- All relevant tests pass, including new tests for the resolver and updated tests for the toolbar actions.
- The client type check and linting for changed files are successful. 

This enhancement improves the user experience by providing quick access to view changes directly from the pull request list.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed all-files mapping, generic editor's collection-wide `Promise.all`, provider's direct per-URI GitHub request, and 3,000-file supported cardinality are all explicit in repository code. Exact latency varies by PR size and network, but the unbounded request count and critical-path wait are not assumptions.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub file-content HTTP requests, decoded file bytes, and text models
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For F changed files, a cold open creates F remote reads for added/removed files and 2F for modified/renamed files; the accepted GitHub limit of 3,000 files therefore reaches roughly 3,000-6,000 unique content requests and models in one aggregate burst.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: The diff editor's initial display is delayed until all remote models settle, while the burst can saturate the network, exhaust GitHub quota, and create severe memory/GC pressure.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, the pull-request row had no action that constructed a multi-diff over every remote PR file, so opening the row did not launch this collection-wide set of GitHub content reads.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new resolver maps the complete changed-file list to one or two `copilot-pr` URIs per file. `MultiDiffEditorInput._createModel` eagerly calls `createModelReference` for both sides of every item and awaits one collection-wide `Promise.all`; the `PRContentProvider` resolves each unique URI with a direct GitHub contents request.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT lines 66-76 newly turn every returned PR file into eager remote model inputs; line 68 constructs each item that the existing multi-diff implementation resolves collection-wide.
Findings.Title: Bound remote file loading before opening the multi-diff
Findings.Impact: Opening or restoring a moderately large PR changes tab can remain blank for a long time and can trigger hundreds or thousands of simultaneous GitHub requests; a new head SHA repeats the cold load because every URI changes.
Findings.Evidence: Added lines 66-76 map every `changes.files` entry to remote `copilot-pr` model URIs. `multiDiffEditorInput.ts:204-254` maps the entire resource array, starts both model references per item, and waits for all promises before publishing documents. `extensions/copilot/.../prContentProvider.ts:93-123` calls `getFileContent` for each URI, which reaches `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}`. The provider has no limiter, and its adaptive fetcher learns throttling per exact pathname only after a response, so unique file paths are not bounded. The added test explicitly models GitHub's 3,000-file response ceiling.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the full resource list but resolve remote models lazily for visible rows, or introduce a shared bounded limiter for `copilot-pr` model/content resolution and publish incrementally instead of awaiting every side at once.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The lowercasing, case-sensitive key construction, existing session poll owner, one-minute cadence, and review pagination are all directly traced. The only magnitude uncertainty is how often recorded GitHub identities contain uppercase characters, which affects severity rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Repeated GitHub pull-request and review-list HTTP requests
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For a mixed-case owner or repository, the extra model polls once per minute for the lifetime of the open editor; each cycle performs a PR GET plus review-list pagination at 100 reviews per page (up to 100 pages), in addition to the session's existing poll.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: An open changes tab unnecessarily consumes network bandwidth and GitHub quota continuously, with cost growing with tab lifetime and review history size.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The session polling contribution held one shared, case-sensitive model key using the PR identity recorded on the session and coalesced all exact-key polling owners onto one scheduler.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new editor URI lowercases owner/repository names, reparses those lowercased values, acquires a model with that different case-sensitive reference key, and starts its own poll loop. When the session identity uses GitHub's permitted mixed casing, this creates a second model instead of sharing the already-polled one.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 118 newly acquires the live model from the lowercased source identity, and line 123 polls it; together with added line 37 this defeats the existing exact-key model/poll coalescing for mixed-case identities.
Findings.Title: Reuse the existing case-insensitive PR poller
Findings.Impact: Opening changes for a session PR such as `UpStream/Project#7` leaves both `UpStream/Project/7` and `upstream/project/7` models polling every minute until the editor closes, duplicating metadata and potentially multi-page review traffic.
Findings.Evidence: `createPullRequestChangesEditorInput` lowercases owner/repo at added line 37, while added line 118 acquires a model from the parsed lowercase URI and line 123 starts polling it. `GitHubService.createPullRequestModelReference` keys `ReferenceCollection` with the case-sensitive `getPullRequestKey`; the existing `GitHubPullRequestPollingContribution` acquires the original session casing and already calls `startPolling`. `GitHubPullRequestModel._refresh` fetches PR metadata and reviews in parallel, and `getReviews` paginates 100 reviews per request. The new casing test explicitly exercises `UpStream/Project` becoming the same lowercase editor URI.
Findings.Recommendation: Normalize owner/repository casing in the shared PR reference-collection key (and related PR model keys), or preserve and resolve the canonical session identity before acquiring the model, so the editor adds a polling reference to the existing model rather than creating another one.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or restore a pull request changes multi-diff
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The editor first waits for PR metadata, merge-base comparison, and the complete changed-file list. It then creates text-model references for every original/modified URI and waits for all of them before publishing the initial document set, so every remote content read is on the initial editor-display critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch PR details before and after loading, compare base/head to obtain merge base, and paginate changed files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two PR GETs, one comparison GET, and ceil(F/100) sequential file-list GETs; for 3,000 files this is 33 requests before content loading.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The row had no changes-editor action and did not perform this request sequence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All must finish before the resolver returns any multi-diff resources.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve each `copilot-pr` text document through the extension-host content provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: K unique provider resolutions, one per existing file side.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No all-files PR multi-diff was created from this row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The generic multi-diff waits for all model-reference promises before publishing documents.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch each file side from GitHub's contents endpoint; large-file responses can add a blob request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: K content GETs, potentially up to 2K when a contents response requires blob fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No collection-wide content fan-out occurred from this action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All K primary resolutions are awaited as one aggregate before initial display.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: F changed files after complete pagination; effective remote-side cardinality K is F for all-added/all-removed PRs and approaches 2F for modified/renamed files. The code accepts complete lists up to GitHub's 3,000-file limit, so K reaches 3,000-6,000.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The comparison and file-list reads run in parallel after the first PR GET; file-list pages are sequential. After resolution, all K model references are launched through nested Promise.all/Promise.allSettled without a shared limiter. The GitHub fetcher's learned throttle is keyed by exact endpoint pathname and is absent for cold unique file paths, so it does not bound this initial aggregate burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The two PR GETs and file list explicitly use noCache; comparison may use the platform provider's normal ETag behavior. Text models coalesce only identical URIs, but every file side is unique. A still-open editor is warm; closing/reopening may reuse model-service lifetime caching, but a new head SHA changes every URI and is fully cold. Provider failures return empty content that can become a cached model rather than a shared negative cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the added all-files URI mapping, multi-diff's eager aggregate model resolution, extension provider's direct per-URI GitHub call, and supported 3,000-file cardinality are all directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact latency, response sizes, and how often users open very large PRs vary, but hundreds-file PRs are realistic and the unbounded K-request mechanism is explicit. This uncertainty affects severity, not mechanism confidence.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable high-severity concurrency burst and boundary fan-out; submitted a finding requiring lazy or bounded remote model resolution.

Scenarios.Scenario: Keep a pull request changes tab open while the PR changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Minute polling is background work and is off the steady-state display critical path. If head/base changes, the resolver performs a fresh metadata/comparison/file-list sequence; prior resources remain cached while refresh runs, but publishing the new resource set triggers another K-side model load before the updated document set is ready.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Poll PR metadata and the complete review list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per model every 60 seconds: one PR GET plus ceil(R/100) review-list GETs, up to 100 review pages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The session polling contribution already owned one model/poller under the session's original casing; no lowercased editor model existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background for an unchanged PR; it drives subsequent refresh when head/base changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload PR metadata, merge base, and changed files after head/base changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per distinct observed head/base change: two PR GETs, one comparison, and ceil(F/100) file-list pages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No open changes editor followed head/base updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the current view's critical path because cached resources remain, but blocks the updated diff state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load all file sides for the updated SHA.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: K newly keyed content requests per distinct head/base update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks publication of the updated multi-diff document set.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Open-tab lifetime, review count R (100 reviews per page), changed-file count F, and number of head/base updates. Mixed-case owner/repo identities determine whether polling is duplicated.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Exact-case model references share one scheduler and one in-flight refresh. The lowercased editor source defeats that coalescing when the session identity has mixed casing, producing two independent minute schedulers. Each refresh runs PR and paginated-review reads in parallel; changed head/base additionally triggers the changes fetch and later unbounded content load.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Unchanged poll results are structurally suppressed and do not refetch the changed-file list. Exact-key model references and refreshes coalesce. Case variants are distinct cache keys. A new commit invalidates all content URIs by SHA, so their model/content cache is cold; refresh failures keep the last successful changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: lowercasing, case-sensitive reference keys, existing session polling ownership, polling cadence, and paginated review reads are explicit and covered by the added mixed-case test.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Mixed-case prevalence and review-history size vary. The duplicate model keys and duplicated minute request sequence are deterministic whenever mixed casing is present.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable missing coalescing for mixed-case PR identities; submitted a medium-severity finding. Exact-case identities reuse the existing poller and do not have this duplicate cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start or restore the workbench without a PR changes editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new BlockRestore contribution constructor registers one resolver before UI restoration. It does not call GitHub or enumerate PRs. The GitHub singleton and multi-diff resolver service are delayed services; registration adds only local service/set bookkeeping.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant per window, independent of session, PR, or file count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No asynchronous work, queue, or boundary operation is started by the contribution constructor.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is read or populated until a matching editor URI is resolved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that no network, filesystem, subprocess, database, or IPC boundary is crossed on this no-editor path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: There is a small constant instantiation/registration cost, but no evidence of measurable startup impact or scaling work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable startup regression; the registration is constant local work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render the pull-request toolbar row and accessibility help without invoking the new action
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Rendering constructs one local action descriptor per PR entry and accessibility help conditionally appends one localized string. Code-review matching performs case-insensitive string comparisons over the workspace's PR references.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of visible PR rows or workspace PR references, normally small; no changed collection-wide boundary is reached until action invocation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing hover/action caches remain in use; no new remote cache is touched.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High after tracing action execution separately from descriptor construction.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for performance; these are small local operations.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression on render/help paths.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 15 changed files and relevant transitive editor, observable, polling, GitHub client, and bundled extension-provider paths. Submitted two findings: unbounded all-file remote content loading and duplicate case-variant PR polling. No concrete startup, render, cleanup-lifecycle, or additional cache-retention regression met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
